submission.natural_language_explanation: The pole fires at the word that pins down a determinate property of something: a spatial or geometric specification of how it is oriented, aimed, aligned or measured (pointed, points, aimed, directed, facing, straight, curved, along, across, toward, up/down, left/right, angle, degrees, parallel, perpendicular, vertical, horizontal, level, aligned, wide), a degree or manner modifier (slightly, sharply, closely, plainly, directly, calmly, fast), a predicate that asserts an exact, definite or complete property (clear, obvious, precise, exact, definite, plain, right, honest, direct, complete), a stated connection between two things (related, linked, connected, corresponding, according to), or a verb that puts a definite mark or measure on something (stamp, mark, measure, label); its peak sits on that word itself and on the 'and' or list comma that immediately follows it when it pairs two such descriptions ('clear and accessible', 'top, right and left sides', 'round, elegant and expressive'). Plain narration carrying none of these words - emotion, colour, material, a single ordinary action - peaks around 0.1-0.3 of max, and a bare 'and' joining two plain clauses is an unreliable cue anywhere from 0.0 to 0.5 of max, so a probe cannot rest on a conjunction alone in either direction.
